title: Chart Rewind: In 1986, Conway Twitty Turned Desperation Into a Country No. 1
summary: 40 at 40: Twitty’s “Desperado Love” established a chart milestone.
body: Conway Twitty started his music career as a pop hitmaker on the all-format Billboard Hot 100 — his “It’s Only Make Believe” topped the chart in November 1958 — before he found his full voice in country, and the last of his 40 chart-topping titles in the genre came from a songwriter who made a similar format change. North Carolina-born Sammy Johns earned national recognition when his recording of “Chevy Van” parked at No. 5 on the Hot 100 in 1975, but he followed that by writing his way into the country market. With “Desperado Love,” co-written by Michael, Johns transformed a negative life period into a win. He was about to lose his house, started drinking to numb his depression, then decided to see if there was a song in all of his misery. He felt desperation, brainstormed that into desperado and took off from there. title: Jason Aldean Guarantees Ronnie Milsap Won’t Be Forgotten ‘Anytime Soon’ With New Song: ‘I Knew Immediately That We Were Going to Cut It’
summary: Billboard looks at the writing and recording behind Jason Aldean's "Anytime Soon."
body: When Jason Aldean performed at the Academy of Country Music Awards in Frisco, Texas, on May 16, 2024, his acoustic version of “Should’ve Been a Cowboy” paid homage to the late Toby Keith. But while he was there, Aldean got an additional opportunity to celebrate another country legend. He received a fresh demo of a new song written by two band members, bassist Tully Kennedy and guitarist Kurt Allison, and he quickly recognized the sound that Allison had created with a Fender Rhodes electric piano. “It was a tip of the hat to Ronnie Milsap,” Aldean remembers. “I knew immediately – one listen – that we were going to cut it, and it was going to make the record.” “Anytime Soon,” released by Broken Bow to country radio on Aug. 2 via PlayMPE, uses a keyboard tone akin to Milsap’s “Stranger in My House,” blended with classic rock sounds that embody Tom Petty and Journey. It was created with Aldean’s musical tastes in mind, as well as his penchant for stories about guys trying to pick themselves up. “There are two things that never go out of style, man: falling in love and relationships falling apart,” Aldean says. “For whatever reason, I’ve always leaned into the latter.” Kennedy an…

title: ‘NCT 127 Is Back’: K-Pop’s Mavericks Talk Contract Renewals & Being Uncompromising in Their ‘Neo’ Sound
summary: The Seoul-based NCT subgroup just hit the 10-year mark. But despite enlistments and an evolving lineup, some things never change.
body: Someone has given NCT 127 notepads. The five bandmates are parked along one side of a wide conference room table, each with hotel stationery and a pen sitting in front of them. It immediately feels like a mistake. When not reflecting on what’s changed for the group in the decade since debut — or heckling each other for misspeaking like they’re still bratty kids living on top of each other in dorms — they’re hunched over, doodling. Just over 10 years ago, the world was introduced to NCT ’s first fixed subgroup (NCT DREAM, WayV and NCT WISH would soon follow) as teenagers getting aggro in science class. In real life, that rowdy energy has dispersed into a mellower campus crush vibe — if you squint, the drawing could almost be confused for diligent note-taking — but the septet’s seventh studio album, Blingy , is just as loud as ever. “I wanted to make a statement,” Chicago native Johnny says: “NCT 127 is back.” K-pop’s noisiest mavericks have had a relatively quiet couple of years. In 2024, group leader Taeyong enlisted in the South Korean military for compulsory service; deep-voiced, dimpled Jaehyun was next to go. By the end of 2025, …

title: Pixel Watch 5 gets its first update, and Gemini is stealing the show
summary: Gemini and hands-free controls get plenty of attention in the first rollout.
body: TL;DR Pixel Watch 5 gets its first update with September security fixes and software improvements. Google highlights Gemini’s personalized, offline, and proactive capabilities on the watch. Expanded hand gestures make navigating the watch faster and more hands-free. Google recently gave Pixel Watch 5 owners something to tinker with by publishing the smartwatch’s factory images . Now, the company is rolling out the watch’s first software update with new security fixes, bumping the firmware from CD5A.260611.008 to CP3A.260905.002. The September update keeps the Pixel Watch 5 on Wear OS 7, based on Android 17, and Google says it will roll out in phases by carrier and device. But this first update has an odd twist. Despite the new firmware build, Google’s extensive changelog mostly reads like a recap of the software features that arrived with the Pixel Watch 5 at launch .

title: Google’s got two big new upgrades for Translate on Android and iOS
summary: Google shares Translate's latest tools for breaking down language barriers.
body: TL;DR Google’s introducing a pair of Translate upgrades: one for Android, and one for iOS Google’s upgrading Live Translate on Android with support for background translations. Apple users are getting access to Translate’s “listening mode” for no-earbud-needed translations. Being able to act as a real-time interpreter is one of Google Translate’s greatest strengths, thanks to its impressive Live Translate mode . Today the company shares the latest ways it’s making that already powerful mode even better. When you’re trying to do something when traveling like check into a hotel, or get information from someone about a destination on a map, it’s easy to run into a bit of a problem — you want to use Live Translate to help you quickly understand the person you’re talking to, but you also need to keep checking info from another app on your phone. Wouldn’t it be great if Live Translate could simply run in the background , so you didn’t need to keep the Translate app on top?

title: Wear OS users can’t get Gemini to control their smart home
summary: A strange Gemini bug is preventing Wear OS users from controlling their smart home.
body: Credit: Tushar Mehta / Android Authority TL;DR Wear OS users are reporting that Gemini has lost the ability to control their smart home devices. When asking Gemini to perform a task, nothing happens, but the assistant will still say it carried out the action. It appears Gemini has no problems controlling devices when a phone or smart speaker is used. Google recently rolled out an update to Gemini for Home that expanded the range of voice commands across media and home device controls. This change also allows you to combine media commands with other types of commands. While that’s great and all, it appears that the assistant also lost a crucial ability for some users around the same time. According to dozens of Wear OS users on Reddit ( 1 , 2 ), Gemini has lost the ability to control smart home devices. When using their smartwatch to ask Gemini to perform a task, nothing happens, but the assistant will still say it carried out the action. According to the original poster, this error occurred across all of their smart devices, including their lights, AC, vacuum, and more.

title: Lunar Occultation of Venus
summary: On Wednesday, June 17, skywatchers across the United States—and parts of Canada—enjoyed a rare event: a daytime lunar occultation of Venus. A lunar occultation occurs when the Moon moves directly in front of another celestial object from our viewpoint on Earth, briefly hiding it from sight. This ti…
body: Venus is seen as it disappears behind the Moon at the start of the occultation on June 17, 2026, from the Mary W. Jackson NASA Headquarters building in Washington NASA/Joel Kowsky On Wednesday, June 17, skywatchers across the United States—and parts of Canada—enjoyed a rare event: a daytime lunar occultation of Venus. A lunar occultation occurs when the Moon moves directly in front of another celestial object from our viewpoint on Earth, briefly hiding it from sight. This time, the Moon slipped in front of Venus for the first of three occultations happening this year, creating a striking daylight moment for those who caught it. If you missed it, there will be two more opportunities to see Venus disappear behind the Moon in 2026: Sept. 14, visible from parts of Asia, Africa, Europe, and western Russia; and Nov. 7, visible from southern South America.

title: SmallRig brings modular mounting to portable power with its new Nano Power Bank series
summary: One of the few power banks designed for your camera gear.
body: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority Most consumer power banks are designed to sit in a pocket or a bag until you need to plug something in. That’s great if you only need to charge your phone, but these don’t work as well when you’re trying to run a camera, a wireless mic, and a monitor off the same battery during a long shoot. There’s rarely a clean way to attach the power bank itself, so you often end up improvising with cable ties, tape, or Velcro straps. The Nano Power Bank series addresses this problem directly. The two models – the Nano 36 and the Nano 72 – in the lineup come with built-in 1/4″-20 threaded holes and dedicated V-mount plates, so they can be attached to camera cages, tripods, gimbals, and other accessories in SmallRig’s existing ecosystem. The power bank becomes part of the rig itself, giving you a tighter setup and making it easier to move between locations.

title: Homemade manufacturing has never become more accessible
summary: HeyGears G1X brings 2D UV printing designs onto surfaces and full-color 3D models, previously inaccessible to most creators.
body: Starting small goes a long way: 2D UV printing You may think full-color 3D printing is a must-have for HeyGears G1X Series , but the G1X Series also offers a pack for 2D UV and 3D Texture Printing, priced at just $2,799 after the limited-time cashback. The first and easiest way to get started with the G1X printer is printing in 2D on over 400 base materials, like plastic, metal, wood, glass, ceramic, leather, acrylic, and more. Have a tile you want with your design on? It’s really easy to do with HeyGears’ slicer, Blueprint Studio: Place your material in the center of the print bed, start a new Project, select your printer, start the Positioning sequence, and the Blueprint Studio software will automatically calibrate and find the edges of your materials on the print bed so you can import your image or design and rescale to your heart’s desire–then hit Print.

title: I refuse to buy a Pixel Watch until Google changes these 5 things
summary: Google makes a compelling Wear OS watch, but it's not perfect.
body: I’ve tried smartwatches from every major brand, and have run nearly 2,000 miles with a smartwatch on my wrist. There are plenty of excellent options on the market — I usually switch between wearing a Garmin, an Apple Watch, or a Galaxy Watch on my wrist. I enjoyed my time trying out OnePlus and Withings watches, too. Google’s Pixel Watch is the one smartwatch model that never felt right, and after playing around with the Pixel Watch 5 in a hands-on session, I’m still not ready to buy one. Google is really starting to tempt me. The domed Actua 360 display looks absolutely gorgeous, especially when paired with a polished silver aluminum case and metal band. The accuracy of the Pixel Watch’s dual-frequency GPS can hang with the best fitness watches on the market. Plus, Google’s fitness and health suite is finally fit to compete with Apple and Samsung’s offerings. Despite all the improvements, I can’t replace my smartwatches with a Pixel Watch until Google makes these five changes.

title: I tested 2 of the best Android foldables of 2026. Here’s how to avoid buying the wrong one
summary: Motorola makes a strong case with the Razr Fold.
body: I love the Galaxy Z Fold 8. It’s a fantastic experience, with a wider cover screen and landscape-dominant inner display that’s ideal for content and multitasking. However, I understand it’s not for everyone. It’s not an inexpensive phone, and people who are paying $1,900 are going to be more demanding. The cameras aren’t flagship-level, and the form factor isn’t for everyone. Thankfully, Motorola has the ideal alternative. Unlike the Z Fold 8 Ultra , it won’t cost you more than the Galaxy Z Fold 8, and it has many of the features buyers love if you’re sold on a more traditional book-style form factor.

title: Reolink’s new security camera has a clever way to address blind spots
summary: Two set of eyes could make home security a whole lot smarter.
body: TL;DR The new Reolink OMVI 2i Ultra uses two cameras, allowing one to capture a wide view while the other tracks and zooms in on a subject. Reolink’s upgraded ReoNeura AI can learn custom scenarios around your home, while the $199.99 Home Hub 2 adds local storage and natural-language video search without a subscription. Reolink is also expanding smart home support and launching the $199.99 TrackFlex WiFi with 4K dual-lens video, auto-tracking, and AI-powered detection. Home security cameras become a lot more important when you have kids or pets running around. Whether you’re checking if your dog is getting into trouble, making sure the kids got home safely, or keeping an eye on a package outside your door, being able to quickly see what’s happening can offer some much-needed peace of mind. That’s where the new Reolink OMVI 2i Ultra could come in handy. Unveiled at IFA 2026 , the wire-free security camera gives you two sets of eyes on the same area — one to capture the bigger picture and another to follow whatever deserves a closer look.

title: Philips Hue’s new TV camera solves a big problem for TV sync lights
summary: Philips Hue is giving you more ways to sync your lights with what you're watching.
body: TL;DR Philips Hue has announced the Hue Play Screen Sync camera and Hue Play HDMI Sync Box 4K. The Screen Sync camera can sync lights with native smart TV apps and broadcast content and is priced at $119.99. The HDMI Sync Box comes with a slimmer profile and a single HDMI input for $149.99. We’ve seen several leaks of upcoming Philips Hue devices over the last couple of months, and the company has finally made almost all of them official. This includes a bunch of new hardware, smart lights , and software updates coming to Philips Hue devices. The Philips Hue Play Screen Sync camera , which leaked a few months ago, is now official. The Hue Play Screen Sync is a plug-and-play device with automatic calibration, so you only need to place it above your TV.

title: The Galaxy S27 Pro could solve Samsung’s biggest problem — if it fixes these 5 things

body: It was somewhere around this time last year that we began seeing leaked renders of a purported Galaxy S26 Pro model, but this obviously didn’t pan out. Once again, we’re seeing fresh rumors that Samsung might introduce a new Pro model with the Galaxy S27 series in early 2027, and the leaks look more plausible this time around. Along with the rumored redesign of the Galaxy S27 Ultra, the new Galaxy S27 Pro is expected to feature the same design, but in a smaller form factor. I’m really excited about this change because Samsung’s non-Ultra phones have suffered from an identity crisis ever since the Galaxy S23 series. The Plus model in the Galaxy S trio has always had an awkward positioning in the lineup, as it was a bit too pricey and lacked the premium features of the Ultra. I don’t see any wiggle room for a fourth model between the current Plus and Ultra phones, which means the S27 Plus will have to give way for the S27 Pro — and I couldn’t be more thrilled.

title: This phone could support a crazy 500mm teleconverter lens for 20x optical zoom
summary: This could also result in ~41x lossless-resolution zoom.

This would beat the vivo X300 Ultra’s 400mm teleconverter, which is equivalent to ~16.6x zoom. We do have concerns about the size and weight of the 500mm lens, though. The vivo X200 Ultra debuted a 200mm teleconverter lens last year, allowing users to take high-quality ~8x zoom photos. We’ve since seen an escalation of the external lens war, with the vivo X300 Ultra now offering a 400mm teleconverter . However, a new leak suggests that HONOR could up the ante. title: The Pixel 11 may not be a lost cause for GrapheneOS after all
summary: A new firmware discovery could change everything for privacy-focused users.
body: TL;DR GrapheneOS found MTE hardware support in the Pixel 11 after earlier concerns. The discovery could keep GrapheneOS support alive for Google’s latest phones. Developers are testing MTE performance before deciding whether support for Pixel 11 is viable. GrapheneOS appeared ready to walk away from the Pixel 11 series just a few days ago. The privacy-focused Android project even warned against buying the phones after discovering they lacked hardware support for Memory Tagging Extension (MTE), a key security feature. But that warning may have been premature: GrapheneOS developers have now found that Pixel 11 phones do have MTE hardware support, giving the project a potential path toward supporting Google’s latest flagships. GrapheneOS shared the news on X , and they made this discovery after Google released Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 , the first beta version to support the Pixel 11 series. Developers examining the new firmware found references indicating the phones have the necessary MTE capability, despite earlier software suggesting otherwise.

There’s no word on pricing, but this SSD could be ideal for ProRes or APV video capture via your phone. Smartphones have become increasingly capable of high-quality video capture. Apple debuted ProRes video on its iPhones years ago, but Android phones have also made major strides thanks to LOG and APV video capture . Now, Lexar has announced an extremely thin SSD that might be the one to get for people who film a ton of high-quality videos on their phones. The Lexar Muse Ultraslim Portable SSD is marketed as the world’s thinnest portable SSD, with the company claiming that it varies from 1mm to 3.8mm thick. The company says it also comes with a magnetic carry sleeve, allowing it to be attached to an iPhone via MagSafe. This should also play nicely with magnet cases on Android phones or magnet-equipped phones like the Pixel 11 range .

title: UGREEN’s new Qi2 power bank has cooling you can see, as well as feel
summary: Check out all the new additions to UGREEN's power solutions.
body: TL;DR UGREEN’s got a bunch of new power solutions debuting, including the first Qi2 magnetic bank with liquid cooling. That’s joined by a set of new 2-in-1 and 3-in-1 chargers ideal for Apple users. Those combo chargers are available in both foldable travel sizes, as well as desktop stands. These days, power solutions aren’t just about capacity and speed. In order to reach the demanding limits we insist upon, more and more often manufacturers must contend with the ever-present specter of heat — not a battery’s best friend. And while we’ve seen plenty of ways to manage heat , you’ve probably never seen any quite like UGREEN’s latest — literally. Plenty of us already know and love the convenience of magnetic Qi2 battery banks , ready to pop right on the back of compatible phones and cases. With small devices like this, there’s not much room to squeeze in bulky cooling systems. In light of that, UGREEN has engineered a clever solution.

However, now that we’ve gotten an early look at how much better Digital Wellbeing could be, it’s going to be difficult to go back. title: AWOL LuxVision brings 4K 120Hz and optical shift to UST projection
summary: High-refresh 4K gets a much more living-room-friendly setup.
body: Credit: AWOL TL;DR AWOL Vision has unveiled the LuxVision, its new flagship ultra-short-throw projector, at IFA 2026. AWOL says it’s the world’s first 4K 120Hz UST projector to also offer optical shift. The LuxVision is rated at 6,000 ISO lumens and launches around October from $5,999. Projectors are great if you want a ridiculously big picture, but setups with ceiling mounts or long cable runs, along with carefully calculated distances, aren’t exactly living-room friendly. Ultra-short-throw projectors solve much of that by sitting just inches from the wall, and AWOL Vision’s new LuxVision aims to eliminate another compromise by bringing true 4K 120Hz output and optical shift to the format. Unveiled at IFA 2026, AWOL bills the LuxVision as the world’s first 4K 120Hz ultra-short-throw projector with optical shift. That combination is the main selling point, as you get the smoother motion of a 120Hz display without giving up the living-room-friendly setup of a UST projector. At the same time, the optical shift gives you more freedom to position the image without compromising its 4K detail.

title: Smartphone prices may be soaring, but Americans are getting off easy
summary: US shoppers have less to worry about than most smartphone buyers.
body: TL;DR US smartphone prices rose just 5%, far less than the 15% global increase. New phones are getting pricier as memory costs squeeze manufacturers worldwide. Shoppers elsewhere face steeper hikes, making the US look surprisingly insulated. If you’ve been grumbling about the price of this year’s flagship phones , you’re not exactly wrong. Samsung, Google, and Motorola have all asked US shoppers to pay more for their latest flagships, with most of the increases landing around the $100 mark. But here’s the thing: It could be a whole lot worse. Counterpoint Research’s latest smartphone price tracker shows that global smartphone retail prices have climbed an average of 15% so far in 2026. More than 40% of smartphone models have seen price hikes this year, while new launches are coming in 25% more expensive than their year-ago counterparts.

title: Puck or stand? Motorola’s answer to Apple’s MagSafe lets you do both
summary: Motorola gave its new magnetic charger a leg up, quite literally.
body: TL;DR Motorola’s new Snap Wireless Charger brings MagSafe-like magnetic charging to compatible Qi2 devices, with speeds of up to 25W. The slim aluminum charger works with magnetic cases and can slot into an optional stand for upright charging. Pricing and availability haven’t been announced yet, but the charger will come in three Pantone color options. Motorola is steadily building out its accessory lineup, and its latest addition could be particularly interesting if you’ve been waiting for the company to properly embrace magnetic wireless charging. At IFA 2026 , Motorola officially unveiled the Snap Wireless Charger, an accessory that recently leaked . The idea will be instantly familiar if you’ve used Apple’s MagSafe or seen Google’s PixelSnap charger . It magnetically snaps onto the back of your phone and delivers up to 25W of wireless charging with compatible Qi2 devices. The magnets keep the charger aligned, and it works through compatible magnetic cases, too.

title: Aurzen’s pocket-sized folding projector gets a Pro upgrade
summary: Aurzen took its coolest projector and made it better.
body: TL;DR Aurzen’s new ZIP Pro builds on the original folding projector with native 1080p resolution, 200 ANSI lumens, and a larger 38Wh battery. The tri-fold projector packs a big-screen experience into a pocketable, 586g design roughly the size of a large power bank. New features include a built-in touchscreen display, dual Bluetooth headphone support, Nintendo Switch projection, and 2.5 hours of playback in ECO mode. We’ve learned to accept that in tech, anything portable will have compromises compared to its tethered counterpart — except phones , of course. Laptops are generally less powerful than desktops, wireless earbuds have the battery constraints that wired earbuds don’t, and projectors are no different. The smaller projectors get, the more features consumers tend to lose, such as brightness, resolution, battery life, and more. Aurzen knows that, and instead of trying to replace your living-room TV, the company’s new projector goes all in on making the big-screen experience as portable as possible.

The Galaxy A55 was the first Samsung phone to support it, before the Galaxy S25 extended it to the flagship lineup. Now, the company appears to be expanding the same convenience to its wearables, with the Galaxy Watch 9 becoming the first Galaxy smartwatch to support seamless updates.
